newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - OCT 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - OCT 2.

text.p: PRAVO - EuroTel lowered its GSM prices yesterday, one day after the competition, RadioMobil, began offering GSM services.
- Skoda's new line of automobiles, the Octavia, was unveiled internationally in Paris yesterday.

- Both Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and Skoda Auto press spokesman Jiri Hrabovsky have denied the auto maker was requested to export more of its new Octavia automobile in order to lower the trade deficit. Between 3,500-4,000 of the expected 5,000 Octavias to be manufactured by the end of the year are expected to be sold on the domestic market, though original plans called for almost all of the new cars to be sold locally.
- The price of wine may increase by 10 crowns by the beginning of next year according to the Josef Vozdecky, the general manager of Bohemia Sekt, Ceskomoravska Vinarska a.s..
- Ceska Keramika posted losses of 68 million crowns in 1995 according to the firm's financial director, Josef Jurcovsky.

- The Czech Republic is in 35th place out of 49 countries in terms of the competitive ability index according to a study undertaken by the World Economic Forum and the Institute for Management Development in Lausanne. This was higher than any other post-communist country.
- EuroTel intends to invest approximately five billion crowns into its GSM mobile phone network according to the company's financial director, Michal Herman.

- The supernational sugar company, Eastern Sugar, intends to increase its market share by increasing output in two of the Czech sugar companies it controls, namely Cukrovar Nemcice and Cukrovar Brodek.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The state budget finished with a slight surplus of 48 million crowns at the end of September according to Eduard Janota from the Ministry of Finance.
- The relatively large increase of the price of diesel fuel will only slightly influence the current inflation rates according to the Czech Statistics Office. -- Prague Newsroom, +42-2-2423-0003
